source_name: Connecting Region / regional trade press coverage of ME bank launches
why_relevant: Regional business media pick up ME bank launch announcements and often add the partner/vendor detail that the bank's own release omits. Serves as both a corroboration layer for bank claims and a discovery layer for launches whose original press release is no longer online.

source_name: eTenderi.me — Montenegrin tender aggregation & alerting service
why_relevant: Commercial Montenegrin tender-aggregation service offering SMS/email/push alerts on newly published tenders, procurement tracking, competitor win analysis, identification of the biggest buyers, and an OCR-searchable archive of State Commission for Control of Public Procurement decisions. As an aggregator it is the fastest single funnel for spotting banking/IT competitions and for reconstructing which vendors keep winning.

source_name: eKapija — Tenderi / Javne nabavke (Montenegro edition)
source_subtype: commercial B2B tender bulletin / business portal
why_relevant: Regional (RS/ME/BA) business portal whose tender service explicitly covers not only state procurement but tenders of commercial companies, awarded contracts and procurement plans — exactly the indirect/private-buyer channel this cell targets. Daily bulletins twice per working day plus Saturday make it a near-real-time feed.

source_name: TenderiLive — Balkan + EU tender database (Montenegro section)
why_relevant: Aggregates tenders for BA/ME/RS plus most EU states with a sector taxonomy that includes IT services, telecommunications and maintenance. Useful for cross-border visibility on group-level competitions run in Slovenia/Croatia/Serbia by the same parents (NLB, OTP, Erste) whose Montenegrin subsidiaries inherit the awarded vendor.

source_name: OTP Bank Nyrt. — Szállítóknak (supplier portal, group parent of CKB Montenegro)
why_relevant: Group-parent sourcing entry point for OTP, owner of CKB Banka (the largest Montenegrin bank). Documents the self-registration form route (vendorman@otpbank.hu), a phased rollout of SAP Ariba for procurement, a Partner Code of Ethics, and DORA-driven ICT security training obligations for supplier staff — i.e. the actual gateway and compliance bar any vendor to CKB must clear.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (EGP) — central sourcing entity
source_subtype: bank group central procurement entity page
why_relevant: EGP manages the entire external spend of all majority-owned Erste Group entities — which includes Erste Bank AD Podgorica. It publishes the standard supplier document set (NDA, Supplier Assessment Questionnaire, Supplier Performance Scorecard, Supplier Sustainability Scorecard, whistleblower procedure) and a group-wide Supplier Code of Conduct, meaning Montenegrin buying is centrally governed from Vienna rather than locally advertised.

source_name: erstegroupprocurement.com — EGP dedicated supplier site
why_relevant: Referenced from the Erste Group page as EGP's own web presence; expected to carry the supplier onboarding process, Supplier Code of Conduct and possibly active sourcing events for the whole group including Montenegro. Not fetched in this run — URL recorded as a lead, not as verified.

source_name: Erste Bank a.d. Novi Sad — Procurement / vendor database (group sibling model)
source_subtype: subsidiary bank procurement page + vendor registration
why_relevant: Concrete, working example of how an Erste Group subsidiary in the region publishes invitations for goods and services annually, runs an online vendor-database registration form, and imposes General Terms and Conditions of Purchase of Erste Group. It is the closest available template for what Erste Bank AD Podgorica does or will do, and it directly reveals categories Erste tenders in the Western Balkans.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica — corporate site (announcements / saopštenja)
why_relevant: No dedicated 'nabavke/dobavljači' section surfaced for the Montenegrin entity in this run; its saopštenja (press releases) stream is nonetheless where vendor go-lives and technology partnerships leak (e.g. its first e-guarantees issuance announcement). Monitor as the local read-out of Vienna-run sourcing.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica — corporate site
why_relevant: Local entity site; the plausible host of any 'javni poziv', 'oglasi' or tender notice the bank chooses to publish locally. No procurement section was surfaced by search in this run — record as a monitoring target, not as a confirmed procurement page.

source_name: CKB Banka (OTP Group) — corporate site and public calls
source_subtype: bank corporate site / public calls & notices
why_relevant: Largest Montenegrin bank, OTP-owned. Evidence found that CKB does issue 'javni poziv' notices (a CKB public call was circulated via its official Facebook channel) and routinely publishes oglasi (property sale notices) through banking media. Its own announcements page is therefore the local end of the OTP sourcing chain and a leak point for competitions not shown on any state portal.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking news portal carrying bank oglasi
why_relevant: Specialist banking media that republishes banks' formal notices verbatim (repeated 'OGLAS CKB banka' items). Private banks that have no procurement webpage still place statutory and commercial notices in media; this is the practical archive of those notices and the cheapest ongoing sweep for bank-issued calls.

source_name: InformacijeCrnaGora.me — 'Javni poziv' notice aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates 'javni poziv' notices from Montenegrin issuers including banks (observed carrying a Razvojna banka Crne Gore public call for a bidding process). Cheap, open, local-language funnel for bank-issued calls that never reach the state e-procurement portal.

source_name: CBCG — Tenderi i oglasi (Central Bank of Montenegro)
why_relevant: The central bank publishes its own tenders and oglasi outside the ordinary state portal flow. For banking IT/payments vendors CBCG is both a buyer (cash handling, payment infrastructure, IT) and the price/vendor benchmark the commercial banks watch. Also hosts the authoritative register of banks used to build the actor map for this cell.

source_name: CEJN — Portal javnih nabavki Crne Gore (state e-procurement)
why_relevant: Baseline against which the indirect route is measured: state-owned and obligated entities publish here, private banks generally do not. Essential for triangulation — a banking-IT vendor seen winning here is the same shortlist private banks draw from, and state-owned Razvojna banka / IRF activity does appear.

source_name: Uprava/Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki — ujn.gov.me (incl. EU tenderi)
why_relevant: Policy authority; hosts an 'EU tenderi' category and the legal framework (Zakon o javnim nabavkama) that determines which Montenegrin entities are obligated buyers — i.e. defines the boundary this cell is built around, and points to appeal-body decisions naming vendors.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — tender information services (incl. NATO tenderi)
source_subtype: chamber of commerce tender service / registry
why_relevant: The Chamber of Economy runs tender-information services for Montenegrin companies, including a registry of firms eligible for NATO tenders and guidance on eligibility verification. Useful for the actor map (which local IT/integrator firms are pre-qualified for regulated buying) and as a channel where B2B procurement bulletins circulate.

source_name: EBRD Client eProcurement Portal (ECEPP) — Montenegro notices
why_relevant: EBRD-financed contracts of EBRD clients — including Montenegrin financial institutions and EBRD-guaranteed programmes with CKB — are procured and noticed exclusively on ECEPP. This is a donor-driven indirect procurement route that bypasses both the state portal and the banks' own websites, and it names consultants and suppliers.

source_name: SAP Business Network Discovery (ex-SAP Ariba Discovery)
why_relevant: OTP Bank states it is progressively moving procurement onto SAP Ariba. Buyer postings surfaced through Business Network Discovery are therefore a plausible future channel where OTP-group (and hence CKB) sourcing events become visible to non-incumbent suppliers, and registering makes the group's competitions reachable at all.

source_name: MontenegroTenders.com — country tender database with alerts
why_relevant: Commercial English-language database claiming daily-updated coverage of Montenegrin tenders and contracts. Useful as a redundancy layer and for English-side searchability of notices that are only issued in Montenegrin; coverage of genuinely private bank tenders is unproven and should be tested before purchase.

source_name: GlobalTenders — Montenegro tenders
why_relevant: Global aggregator with a Montenegro country page and separate government-tender view; sector filters allow banking/IT slicing and it also indexes IFI-funded notices. Redundancy and cross-check source rather than a primary one.

source_name: TendersInfo — Montenegro tenders (incl. private tenders) & EBRD funding-agency feed
why_relevant: Markets both government and private tenders for Montenegro plus a dedicated EBRD funding-agency listing, with customised email alerts for paid members. The claimed private-tender coverage is the specific reason to evaluate it for this cell.

source_name: TendersOnTime — Montenegro tenders + EBRD tenders
why_relevant: Another global procurement-intelligence platform indexing Montenegro and EBRD notices; offers a free tier useful for low-cost cross-verification that a notice found elsewhere is real and current.

source_name: Addiko Bank Crna Gora — corporate site
why_relevant: Addiko Group subsidiary active in ME; a lean, digitally-focused bank and therefore a live buyer of digital-channel and card technology. No procurement or supplier page was found in this run — monitored as a candidate host for javni poziv notices and as an actor in the map.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka / Lovćen banka / Prva banka / Universal Capital Bank / Adriatic Bank / Ziraat Bank Montenegro — domestic private-bank sites
why_relevant: CBCG's 'Banke u Crnoj Gori' link list is the authoritative roster for building the buyer actor map of this cell. These domestically-owned banks have no group sourcing portal above them, so any tender they run surfaces only on their own site, in press oglasi, or by direct invitation — making the roster the crawl seed for the whole indirect route.

source_name: nabavke.com — CeJN document mirror and tender aggregator (Crna Gora)
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that mirrors CeJN tender documents as directly fetchable PDFs under a stable path (https://www.nabavke.com/tdoc-cejn/documents/{cejnId}-{YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM}-{DocName}.pdf) and exposes per-tender HTML pages with buyer, object, city and an internal id. This is the practical workaround for the CeJN SPA: observed real award documents for Centralna banka Crne Gore, Ministarstvo finansija (SAP Trezor maintenance), CEDIS, Glavni grad Podgorica (smart POS terminal validators). Also claims coverage of bank and private-sector tenders and below-threshold purchases.

source_name: Centralna banka Crne Gore — Tenderi i oglasi
why_relevant: CBCG is both regulator and a contracting authority that buys cash-handling, banknote processing, IT, security and payment-infrastructure goods and services (it also operates the national RTGS/DNS payment system). Its own tender page plus its CeJN filings identify suppliers selling directly into the central bank — the highest-signal single buyer in the ME payments stack.
